body.statement: Can \(\mathsf H_{\mathrm{loc}}\) be developed into a randomized algorithm running in time polynomial in \(n\) and \(d\) that, on the graph event of Theorem 1, evaluates \(\widehat\tau_G\) and returns an observable certificate \(U_G\) satisfying \[R_2(G)\le U_G\le C r(n,d)\] with probability \(1-o(1)\), while its approximation error contributes \(o(r(n,d))\) uniformly over \(\mathcal M_2(G)\)?
body.justification: Exact finite enumeration proves evaluability but does not yet deliver the scalable estimator and certificate needed for large networks.
body.gap: Balanced fixed-slice sampling has known complexity barriers on general bipartite graphs, while the structured random-regular GATE conflict graph and approximate covariance-action target remain untreated.
body.consumer: A successful compiler would turn the minimax theorem into a deployable alternative to graph-cluster randomization with an auditable precision bound.

obligation.what_is_open: Construct a polynomial-time observable approximation to the Rao--Blackwell weights and an operator-norm risk certificate with uniform \(o(r(n,d))\) error.
obligation.obstruction: Finite enumeration is exact but exponential.  Pointwise Monte Carlo evaluation of inclusions or covariance entries does not furnish the relative and operator-norm accuracy needed uniformly over the endpoint \(L^2\) ball, and the frozen handle supplies no contraction, mixing-time, or approximate-counting guarantee.
obligation.attempted: I reduced the requested guarantee to simultaneous inclusion estimation, randomized quadratic-form probing, and evaluation of a finite conditional-expectation ratio.  The first two are pointwise estimable, but converting them to the advertised uniform risk error and evaluating the conditional ratio in polynomial time remain unproved.
obligation.partial_result: The finite evaluator supplies an exact algorithm by enumeration, and Monte Carlo draws from \(\mathsf D_G^{\mathrm{cap}}\) can estimate each \(\pi_u\) and every bilinear form \(x^{\mathsf T}\Gamma_Gx\) pointwise.  What is not proved is a polynomial sample bound uniform over all \(2n\) inclusion probabilities and the operator norm at the relative accuracy needed when \(k/n\asymp\log(d)/d^2\), nor a polynomial procedure for the conditional Rao--Blackwell ratio (8).  In particular, an additive entrywise Monte Carlo guarantee does not imply an \(o(r(n,d))\) worst-case quadratic-form error over the endpoint \(L^2\) ball; that conversion would require operator-norm error \(o(nr(n,d))\).
